recipes.name: Beef Stroganoff 1
instructions: Slice meat into thin strips about 1½ inches wide and 2-3 inches long. Sprinkle lightly with tenderizer, toss and refrigerate.

Cut off mushroom stems even with the caps and slice mushrooms. Sauté ¼ of the onions in 3 Tbs. butter until almost clear, but not brown. Add ¼ of the mushrooms and sauté until just tender. Remove to a 12 quart enamel roasting pan.
Sauté remaining onions and mushrooms in same manner, i.e., in four batches. You may need to add a little butter each time.
In same skillet in which vegetables have been cooked, brown meat a little at a time with a minimum of butter, removing it to the roasting pan as it browns.
Put in 2 cans of bouillon and the flour in a blender and blend until smooth. Set aside.
Pour remaining cans of bouillon into skillet and stir and scrape to deglaze the pan. Add bouillon and flour mixture, stirring as you add to keep smooth.
Add tomato juice and Rhine wine. Pour over the meat and vegetables in roasting pan. Season to taste.
About 1½ hours before serving, place in a 375 degree oven and bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally.
Just before serving, add sour cream and a splash of Rhine wine. Serve with buttered noodles or long grain and wild rice.
recipes.notes: Can easily be halved. Great recipe for a crowd. 375°F oven, 12 quart enamel roasting pan.

recipes.name: Beef Stroganoff 2

ingredients.name: bouillon or consommé (10½ oz can), diluted to make 2 cups

instructions: Sauté mushrooms and onion in 2 tbsp. butter and remove from pan.
Remove fat and bone from steak. Cut into strips 2½" long and ¾" wide.
Melt additional 2 tbsp. butter in pan. Toss strips of meat in flour, coating thoroughly. Brown meat in butter.
Add salt and bouillon-water mixture. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until meat is tender, about 1¼ hours.
Add mushrooms, onions and sour cream; heat. Serve over noodles or rice.
recipes.notes: Uses round steak — more economical cut. Simple, classic version.

recipes.name: Beef Stroganoff 3

ingredients.name: beef tenderloin or boneless top loin steak (½ inch thick)

instructions: Cut beef across grain into about 1½ x ½ inch strips. (Beef is easier to cut if partially frozen, about 1 hour.)
Melt margarine in 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Cook beef in margarine, stirring occasionally, until brown.
Reserve ⅓ cup of the broth. Stir remaining broth, the ketchup, salt and garlic into skillet. Heat to boiling; reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer about 10 minutes or until beef is tender.
Stir in mushrooms and onion. Cover and simmer about 5 minutes or until onion is tender.
Shake reserved broth and the flour in tightly covered container; gradually stir into beef mixture. Heat to boiling, stirring constantly. Boil and stir 1 minute; reduce heat to low.
Stir in sour cream; cook until hot. Serve over noodles.
recipes.notes: Quickest of the three stroganoff versions. 300 cal per serving. Lighter version: decrease margarine to 1 tbsp, use nonstick skillet and reduced-fat sour cream/yogurt for 265 cal.

recipes.name: Beef and Beer Stew
instructions: In large bowl combine flour, 2½ tsp. salt, and pepper. Add chuck, tossing to coat. Set aside.
Heat ¼ cup oil in 4 quart Dutch oven or kettle. In oil, sauté onion and garlic until tender, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from Dutch oven.
Heat remaining oil. Add chuck, brown well on all sides.
Return onion and garlic to Dutch oven, along with beer, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, steak sauce, bay leaves, and thyme. Mix well. Bring mixture to boiling.
Reduce heat; simmer, covered 2 hours or until meat is tender.
Meanwhile, pare potatoes, cut into quarters. Add potatoes and 1 tsp. salt to 1 inch boiling water; simmer, covered 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Drain potatoes well. Toss with parsley. To serve, turn stew mixture into serving dish. Surround the stew with potatoes.
recipes.notes: Dutch oven recipe. Low and slow — hearty and rich.

recipes.name: Stay-A-Bed Stew

ingredients.name: cream of tomato soup (10¾ oz can)

instructions: Mix all ingredients together in a large casserole dish and cover tightly.
Put casserole in 275 degree oven. Let cook for 5 hours, without checking.
recipes.notes: Can also be cooked in a crock pot. 275°F, 2-3 quart casserole dish, covered. True set-it-and-forget-it.

recipes.name: Jordan Marsh's Blueberry Muffins
recipes.source: Cookbook — adapted from Marion Cunningham / Bridge Creek Restaurant, Berkeley, CA (1987)
instructions: Heat the oven to 375 degrees. Grease 12 large muffin cups. Sift together the flour, salt, and baking powder.

Cream the butter and 1¼ cups sugar in a large bowl until light. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Add to the flour mixture alternately with the milk, beating just until smooth.
Crush ½ cup blueberries with a fork, and mix into the batter. Fold in the remaining whole berries.

Fill the muffin cups with batter. Sprinkle the remaining tablespoon of sugar over the tops of the muffins. Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 30 minutes. Cool for 30 minutes before removing from the pan.
Store uncovered, or the muffins will be too moist the second day — if they last that long.
recipes.notes: The trick is crushing some of the blueberries and folding them in — distributes blueberry flavor throughout. Legendary department store recipe from Jordan Marsh in Boston.

recipes.name: Apple, Peach or Plum Cake Cockaigne

ingredients.name: milk (enough to make ½ cup with egg and vanilla)
sliced pared apples, peaches, or unpared plums

instructions: Preheat oven to 425°. If the fruit used is very juicy, reduce the liquid in the dough by at least 1 tablespoon.
Sift before measuring: 1 cup all-purpose flour. Resift with baking powder, ¼ tsp salt, and 2 tbsp sugar.
Add 1½ to 3 tablespoons butter. Work these ingredients like pastry.
Beat well in a measuring cup: 1 egg and ½ tsp vanilla. Add enough milk to make a ½-cup mixture.

Combine with the flour and butter to make a stiff dough. Pat the dough into the pan with a floured palm or spread with a spoon, then distribute evenly by pushing with the fruit sections as you place them closely in overlapping rows.
Arrange 3 to 4 cups sliced fruit in overlapping rows on the dough.
Sprinkle with a mixture of about 1 cup sugar, 2 teaspoons cinnamon, and 3 tablespoons melted butter.
Bake about 25 minutes.
recipes.notes: Joy of Cooking classic — 'Cockaigne' denotes a personal favorite of the authors. Works with apples, peaches, or plums. 9x9x2½ inch pan.

recipes.name: Swedish Meatballs
instructions: Put everything in a bowl together and mix it to an even batter (it should NOT be runny!).
Grab a pinch of the mixture and roll it until it resembles a meatball. Repeat until you've used all the mixture.
Put them in a frying pan on medium heat, fry evenly until cooked through.
recipes.notes: Grandma didn't write down spice measurements — start small, make one and taste it, adjust from there. Tip: wet your hands when rolling and they won't stick. 500g ≈ 1.1 lbs.

recipes.name: Elizabeth Frink's Roast Lemon Chicken
recipes.source: NYT Cookbook — from The Artists' and Writers' Cookbook
instructions: Heat the oven to 325 degrees. Place the chicken in a large baking dish and season inside and out with salt and pepper.

Remove the skin from 1 lemon in strips with a vegetable peeler, and rub the skin over the outside of the chicken. Quarter the lemon and squeeze the juice over and into the chicken. Put the lemon pieces and garlic cloves inside the cavity.

Melt the butter with the olive oil in a small pan. Pour about one-third of the butter mixture inside the chicken. Tie the legs together with kitchen string. Pour the remaining butter and oil over the chicken. Re-season the top.
Roast the chicken for 1½ hours, or until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the leg registers 165 degrees, basting every 15 minutes with the pan juices.
Half an hour before the chicken is done, pour the juice from the second lemon over the chicken and sprinkle with the parsley.

Transfer the chicken to a cutting board to sit for 15 minutes before carving. Pour ½ cup water or broth into the roasting pan and place it over high heat. Scrape up the pan drippings with a wooden spoon. Reduce the pan juices to the desired consistency, and season to taste.
Carve and serve the chicken, passing the sauce on the side.
recipes.notes: The technique is all about repetitions of lemon — peel on skin, juice over, pieces in cavity, second lemon 30 min before done. Great cold too — makes excellent sandwiches on brioche.

recipes.name: Roasted Broccoli with Butter and Mustard

ingredients.name: broccoli, cut into 1½ to 2-inch florets, stems sliced ¼-inch thick

instructions: Heat the oven to 450 degrees. On a baking sheet, toss the broccoli with the olive oil, salt and pepper. Arrange in a single layer, cut-sides down, and roast, without flipping, until browned and crisp-tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Add the butter, vinegar and mustard to the broccoli on the sheet pan and toss until the butter's melted, scraping up browned bits from the pan as you go. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
recipes.notes: Dead simple side dish. The butter-vinegar-mustard combo on roasted broccoli is surprisingly good.

recipes.name: La Scala Chopped Salad

ingredients.name: grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese

instructions: Add all dressing ingredients (olive oil, red wine vinegar, garlic, Dijon mustard, salt, pepper, and Pecorino Romano) to a small bowl or jar. Whisk together or seal and shake to combine.
In a large bowl, combine shredded iceberg lettuce, romaine lettuce, chickpeas, Italian salami, and mozzarella cheese.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss to coat. Serve immediately. Store leftovers in the fridge for 1-2 days; keep dressing separate if prepping in advance.
recipes.notes: A copycat of the famous La Scala Beverly Hills chopped salad. Can substitute dry mustard (1 tsp) for Dijon (3 tsp). Dress separately to prep ahead.

recipes.name: Roasted Sweet Potato Salad with Lentils

ingredients.name: sea salt and pepper to taste

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Slice sweet potatoes into small wedges and place on baking sheet. Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, toss to coat. Sprinkle with cumin, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper; toss again.
Bake sweet potatoes for 45-55 minutes total.
While sweet potatoes bake, cook lentils: bring 3 cups water to boil, add lentils, reduce to simmer, cook covered 4 minutes. Remove from heat and leave covered 2-3 more minutes. Drain.
Prep garlic: slice top off half bulb, drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil and pinch of salt. Wrap tightly in parchment or foil.

When 20 minutes remain on sweet potatoes, remove from oven. Add drained lentils and toss with sweet potatoes. Place wrapped garlic bulb in corner of baking sheet. Return to oven for 20 more minutes until garlic is aromatic and sweet potatoes are caramelized.
Make dressing: whisk together parsley, tahini, lime juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add 4-5 tbsp water and whisk to desired consistency.
When done baking, squeeze roasted garlic into dressing and whisk until combined.

Add sweet potatoes and lentils to a large bowl. Drizzle with half the tahini dressing and toss. Top with chopped almonds, capers, and fresh parsley. Drizzle remaining dressing on top. Serve immediately.
Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days.
recipes.notes: Can use pre-cooked or canned lentils to save time. Cashew butter can substitute for tahini for a milder, sweeter flavor. Add kale, zucchini, or Brussels sprouts to the baking sheet in the last 20 minutes for extra greens.

recipes.name: Honey Mustard Quinoa Apple Salad with Crispy Shallots
instructions: Add quinoa to a medium saucepan and cover with stock. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook until all liquid is absorbed, about 15-20 minutes. Transfer to a bowl to cool.
While quinoa cooks, fry shallots: combine sliced shallots and 1/3 cup olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook 15-20 minutes until golden and crispy, stirring often. Remove from heat.
Place a sieve over a small bowl and pour in shallots, separating oil from shallots. Transfer shallots to a paper towel-lined plate and sprinkle with salt. Let oil cool at least 5 minutes.
Make vinaigrette: whisk apple cider vinegar, honey, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper into the slightly cooled shallot oil. Taste and adjust seasoning.

In a large salad bowl, combine cooled quinoa, arugula, parsley, apple slices, pepitas, and fried shallots. Drizzle vinaigrette over top and toss to combine. Grind extra black pepper on top. Top with Parmesan and enjoy.
recipes.notes: Use a sharp, crisp apple like Honeycrisp or Granny Smith. Swap pepitas for walnuts, pecans, or almonds. To make vegan, use vegetable stock and skip or sub dairy-free Parmesan. If meal-prepping, add apple fresh just before serving to prevent browning.

recipes.name: Tuscan Chicken and Spaghetti Squash

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken, cut into bite-size pieces
sun-dried tomatoes, packed in oil, drained, julienne cut

instructions: Cook spaghetti squash: pierce squash several times with a knife, place on a microwave-safe plate, and microwave on high 8-12 minutes until tender. Let cool. (Alternative: roast at 350°F for 45-60 min cut-side down.)

Season chicken with salt, pepper, and Italian seasoning. Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook 5-7 minutes until golden and cooked through (165°F internal temp). Remove to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 1 tbsp butter to pan. Add shallot and garlic; cook until softened, about 2-3 minutes.
Add sun-dried tomatoes and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer.
Turn off heat. Stir in Parmesan cheese and spinach until wilted. Add chicken and any accumulated juices back to the pan.
Cut cooled squash in half lengthwise, remove seeds, and scrape out strands with a fork. Stir squash into cream sauce until evenly coated.
Garnish with fresh parsley if desired and serve immediately.
recipes.notes: Low carb and gluten free. Spaghetti squash can be cooked ahead of time and reheated. Look for julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes at the store to save prep time. Recipe assembled from Punchfork and search snippets — original page had a fetch error.

recipes.name: Whole Roasted Cauliflower with Pistachio Pesto

ingredients.name: small yellow onions, sliced 1/4 inch thick lengthwise
cilantro and flat-leaf parsley leaves, lightly packed

instructions: Position a rack in the center of the oven and heat to 400°F.
Trim cauliflower stem flush with the head so it sits flat.

Heat a 10-inch cast-iron or heavy ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tbsp olive oil, onions, and 1/4 tsp salt. Cook, stirring, until translucent and golden at edges, 7-10 minutes. Stir in 3/4 cup water and remove from heat.

Rub cauliflower with remaining 1 tbsp oil, then pepper and remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Clear the center of the skillet and nestle the cauliflower in it. Cover pan tightly with foil and bake until a paring knife meets no resistance when inserted, 20-30 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the pesto: reserve a bit of lemon zest for garnish. Place remaining zest in a food processor with the herbs, 1/4 cup olive oil, pistachios, garlic, salt, and pepper. Pulse until well combined.

Turn oven to 450°F (or 425°F convection). Uncover cauliflower and baste with pan juices. Cook, basting occasionally and adding 1/4 cup water if pan threatens to dry out, until nicely browned, 20-30 more minutes.
Spoon pesto over top, sprinkle with reserved lemon zest and more fresh herbs, and serve.
recipes.notes: Recipe is paywalled on NYT Cooking — assembled from multiple third-party sources. Orange cauliflower preferred but any color works. Pine nuts or almonds can substitute for pistachios. The cauliflower becomes almost custardy — serve with a spoon. Works great in a Dutch oven for the covered portion.
